summary: Earth Jukebox is an innovative web tool that transforms NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) data into live sound, making climate information accessible to blind and low-vision users, as well as those on low-end devices. Users can select themes like sea ice or CO2 and hear corresponding sounds based on real-time data. The system employs a 32x16 grid for sound generation, ensuring low energy consumption, as all processing occurs locally in the browser without heavy streaming. The project aims to enhance engagement with climate data while minimizing its ecological footprint, advancing inclusivity in Earth science communication.
details:
EARTH JUKEBOX

Earth Jukebox is an innovative tool that translates NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) visuals into sound, allowing users to select themes like sea ice or CO2 and listen as data points are mapped to audio. Key features include individual sound mappings—warmer areas create higher pitches, CO2 increases tempo, and rainfall resembles a patter. Accessibility is prioritized for blind and low-vision users, supporting keyboard controls and captions. This low-carbon tool runs locally on devices with minimal data usage, enabling offline functionality and multilingual support. Designed to enhance understanding of climate data, it uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and the Web Audio API, with planned user testing and open-source release for broader outreach. The initiative emphasizes music-like representations of data, making complex trends easier to grasp.
